The 32.3m surpasses those caused by disasters for the first time, as 82.2m people displaced in total around world The number of internal displacements triggered by conflict or violence around the world reached a record high in 2025, surpassing the number of disaster-driven internal displacements for the first time. A report published by the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) shows that by the end of 2025 there were 32.3m conflict-driven internal displacements. That is 60% higher than those recorded the previous year, and – for the first time since data collection began in 2008 – above displacements driven by natural disasters, which reached 29.9m in 2025. Jan Egeland, the secretary general of the Norwegian Refugee Council, described the figures as a “sign of a global collapse” in basic protection of civilians.

Conflict and violence drove more people to flee within their own countries last year than natural and manmade disasters for the first time on record, monitors said on May 12. The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre and the Norwegian Refugee Council said in their annual report on the subject that at the end of 2025, 82.2 million people were living in internal displacement worldwide. The figure is just under the highest number ever recorded in 2024. "Numbers remain at historic highs," the director of the IDMC, Tracy Lucas, told AFP, calling the trends "a wake-up call". Over the course of last year, 65.8 million new internal displacements were reported, including a number of people forced to flee multiple times, the report showed.

Conflict and violence were responsible for 32.3 million of those displacements -- up 60 percent from a year earlier -- while 29.9 million fled storms, floods and other disasters. "Never have we recorded such a staggering number of displacements related to conflict," said Lucas. The report detailed how emerging, escalating and entrenched conflicts in places such as Iran and the Democratic Republic of Congo forced people to flee repeatedly within their countries. Such displacements remain highly concentrated. As they were hit by deepening instability last year, Iran and the DR Congo alone accounted for two-thirds of all new conflict-driven internal displacements, counting around 10 million each, the report said. Of the 69.7 million people who at the end of 2025 were living in internal displacement because of conflicts across 54 countries, nearly half were in just five countries, it said.

The number of internal displacements triggered by conflict or violence around the world reached a record high in 2025, surpassing the number of disaster-driven internal displacements for the first time.

A report published by the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) shows that by the end of 2025 there were 32.3m conflict-driven internal displacements. More than 83% of the people displaced in 2025 were forced to flee their homes in their countries because of conflict and violence, with the remainder having left because of natural disasters.

payload.title: Väkivalta ja konfliktit ajoivat ennätysmäärän ihmisiä pakoon kotimaissaan vuonna 2025
payload.summary: Konfliktien ja väkivallan aiheuttamat sisäiset siirtymiset nousivat vuonna 2025 ennätyslukemiin ja ylittivät ensi kertaa katastrofien aiheuttamat siirtymiset.
payload.content:
Väkivalta ja konfliktit ajoivat vuonna 2025 ennätysmäärän ihmisiä pakenemaan kotimaidensa rajojen sisällä, käy ilmi Internal Displacement Monitoring Centren ja Norwegian Refugee Councilin vuosiraportista. Vuoden aikana kirjattiin 32,3 miljoonaa konfliktien ja väkivallan aiheuttamaa sisäistä siirtymistä, mikä oli 60 prosenttia enemmän kuin edellisvuonna.

## Konfliktit ohittivat katastrofit ensi kertaa

Raportin mukaan konfliktien ja väkivallan aiheuttamat siirtymiset ylittivät ensimmäistä kertaa luonnonkatastrofien ja muiden katastrofien aiheuttamat sisäiset siirtymiset sen jälkeen, kun vertailukelpoista seurantaa alettiin tehdä vuonna 2008. Katastrofit, kuten myrskyt ja tulvat, aiheuttivat vuonna 2025 yhteensä 29,9 miljoonaa sisäistä siirtymistä.

Kaikkiaan vuoden aikana raportoitiin 65,8 miljoonaa uutta sisäistä siirtymistä. Luku voi sisältää samoja ihmisiä useammin kuin kerran, jos he ovat joutuneet pakenemaan toistuvasti. Vuoden 2025 lopussa maailmassa eli 82,2 miljoonaa ihmistä sisäisessä pakolaisuudessa. Määrä jäi hieman alle vuoden 2024 kaikkien aikojen korkeimman kokonaisluvun, mutta pysyi historiallisesti erittäin korkealla tasolla.

## Siirtymiset keskittyivät voimakkaasti

Raportissa korostuu, että konfliktiperäinen sisäinen pakolaisuus ei jakaudu tasaisesti eri puolille maailmaa. Vuoden 2025 lopussa 69,7 miljoonaa ihmistä eli konfliktien vuoksi sisäisessä pakolaisuudessa 54 maassa, ja lähes puolet heistä oli vain viidessä maassa.

Uusista konfliktien aiheuttamista sisäisistä siirtymisistä suuri osa keskittyi Iraniin ja Kongon demokraattiseen tasavaltaan. Raportin mukaan nämä kaksi maata vastasivat yhteensä noin kahdesta kolmasosasta kaikista uusista konfliktiperäisistä sisäisistä siirtymisistä, ja kummassakin kirjattiin noin 10 miljoonaa siirtymistä.

IDMC:n johtaja Tracy Lucas kuvasi kehitystä vakavaksi varoitukseksi. Norwegian Refugee Councilin pääsihteeri Jan Egeland puolestaan katsoi lukujen kertovan siviilien perussuojelun maailmanlaajuisesta romahduksesta. Raportin perusteella erityisen huolestuttavaa on se, että pitkittyvät, kärjistyvät ja uudet konfliktit pakottavat samoja ihmisiä liikkeelle yhä uudelleen omien maidensa sisällä.
summary_bullets: Konfliktit ja väkivalta aiheuttivat 32,3 miljoonaa sisäistä siirtymistä vuonna 2025.
Luku oli 60 prosenttia suurempi kuin vuotta aiemmin ja ylitti ensi kertaa katastrofien aiheuttamat siirtymiset.
Vuoden 2025 lopussa 82,2 miljoonaa ihmistä eli sisäisessä pakolaisuudessa eri puolilla maailmaa.

The 32.3m surpasses those caused by disasters for the first time, as 82.2m people displaced in total around world The number of internal displacements triggered by conflict or violence around the world reached a record high in 2025, surpassing the number of disaster-driven internal displacements for the first time. A report published by the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) shows that by the end of 2025 there were 32.3m conflict-driven internal displacements. That is 60% higher than those recorded the previous year, and – for the first time since data collection began in 2008 – above displacements driven by natural disasters, which reached 29.9m in 2025. Jan Egeland, the secretary general of the Norwegian Refugee Council, described the figures as a “sign of a global collapse” in basic protection of civilians.

Conflict and violence drove more people to flee within their own countries last year than natural and manmade disasters for the first time on record, monitors said on May 12. The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre and the Norwegian Refugee Council said in their annual report on the subject that at the end of 2025, 82.2 million people were living in internal displacement worldwide. The figure is just under the highest number ever recorded in 2024. "Numbers remain at historic highs," the director of the IDMC, Tracy Lucas, told AFP, calling the trends "a wake-up call". Over the course of last year, 65.8 million new internal displacements were reported, including a number of people forced to flee multiple times, the report showed.

Conflict and violence were responsible for 32.3 million of those displacements -- up 60 percent from a year earlier -- while 29.9 million fled storms, floods and other disasters. "Never have we recorded such a staggering number of displacements related to conflict," said Lucas. The report detailed how emerging, escalating and entrenched conflicts in places such as Iran and the Democratic Republic of Congo forced people to flee repeatedly within their countries. Such displacements remain highly concentrated. As they were hit by deepening instability last year, Iran and the DR Congo alone accounted for two-thirds of all new conflict-driven internal displacements, counting around 10 million each, the report said. Of the 69.7 million people who at the end of 2025 were living in internal displacement because of conflicts across 54 countries, nearly half were in just five countries, it said.
